title: How far must capital costs move to flip the sand-store versus heat-pump verdict, and is that more than the price year moves it?
summary: Scales the PyPSA technology-data capital costs in the cost model of energy-thermal-real and bisects for the multiplier at which a house-sized sand store and an air-source heat pump cost the same, on real German day-ahead prices 2015–2019. The table’s capex is in 2025 euros and the prices are nominal; deflated to the price year with Eurostat HICP (factor 0.76–0.80), weekly cycling at house scale goes to the heat pump in all five years (margin +0.003 to +0.019 EUR/kWh), because capital is a larger part of the pump’s cost of heat. Daily cycling survives at house scale in all five years and district weekly in four. On the original mixed basis, weekly cycling flips at 1.16, 1.20, 1.20, 0.59 and 1.02 times the store’s table capex, and the spread across price years (sd 0.0063 EUR/kWh) exceeds the cost spread at h = 0.10 (0.0039). Five years, capex only, wholesale prices; h is an assumption, labelled; all other inputs are sourced.
lede: does a sand heat store beat a heat pump once costs and prices are in the same euros? Weekly cycling at house scale goes to the heat pump in all five years (2015 to 2019); daily cycling still favours the store.
